defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 8 Documentation of administration of medication Each medication administered by the assisted living facility staff must be documented in the resident's record. The documentation must include the signature and title of the person who administered the medication. The documentation must include the medication name, dosage, date and time administered, and method and route of administration. The staff must document the reason why medication administration was not completed as prescribed and document any follow-up procedures that were provided to meet the resident's needs when medication was not administered as prescribed and in compliance with the resident's medication management plan.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure medications were administered as ordered for one of four residents (R2) who received medication management services. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death), and was issued at an isolated scope (when one or a limited number of residents are affected or one or a limited number of staff are involved or the situation has occurred only occasionally). The findings include: R2 was admitted on October 14, 2024, with diagnoses that included diabetes. R2's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as the service plan) dated March 3, 2025, indicated R2 received services to include medication administration. R2's signed prescriber orders included: -Lantus Solostar Pen 100 units/milliliter (ml); inject 23 units daily at bedtime (diabetes), order dated July 21, 2025 -Please administer all insulin following meals. HOLD insulin if patient (R2) does not eat, order dated July 23, 2025 R2's medication administration record (MAR) dated August 2025, included the following: -Lantus Solostar injection 100 units/ml; inject 23 units subcutaneously at bedtime. -administer all insulin following meals. Hold insulin if resident does not eat. On August 12, 2025, at 7:24 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-F administer oral medications and check R1's blood sugar. ULP-F stated R2 had scheduled insulin; however, it was not administered until after he started eating his meal. On August 12, 2025, at 9:14 a.m., ULP-F removed R2's insulin pen from the medication cart and prepare it for administration without verifying the order in the electronic medication administration record (EMAR). ULP-F read the label on the insulin pen which indicated to administer 18 units. ULP-F dialed the insulin pen to 18 units and brought it to R2 in the dining room where he administered the insulin into R2's abdomen. ULP-F returned to the medication cart and documented the administration under the order that indicated "administer all insulin following meals. Hold insulin if resident does not eat". On August 12, 2025, at 9:30 a.m., the surveyor reviewed R2's medications listed on the MAR with signed prescriber orders. R2's MAR did not include an order for Lantus 18 units. R2's record lacked prescriber orders for Lantus 18 units. The surveyor met with licensed practical nurse (LPN)-H and inquired about R2's Lantus insulin orders. LPN-H reviewed R2's MAR and prescriber orders and stated R2 received insulin once daily at bedtime. LPN-H stated R2's current Lantus insulin order was to administer 23 units at bedtime. LPN-H stated he was unsure why R2's MAR had an order stating "administer all insulin following meals. Hold insulin if resident does not eat". LPN-H stated ULP-F usually worked the evening shift and would administer R2's insulin at bedtime. LPN-H stated he would assess R2 and update R2's primary care provider on the error. On August 12, 2025, at 10:10 a.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated she had spoken with LPN-H regarding ULP-F administering 18 units of Lantus insulin to R2. CNS-B stated R2's Lantus insulin pen label was incorrect. CNS-B stated R2 used to receive 18 units at bedtime, but that order had changed and was updated in R2's MAR however, the label was not updated to reflect the dose change. CNS-B stated she could see how the order stating to administer all insulin following meals could be confusing to the ULP, especially since R2 only received insulin at bedtime. The licensee's Medication Management Plan policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the RN ensured that direct care staff and medication aides were trained on each resident's plan including administration instructions and monitoring requirements. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 9 Documentation of medication setup Documentation of dates of medication setup, name of medication, quantity of dose, times to be administered, route of administration, and name of person completing medication setup must be done at the time of setup.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure documentation of medication setup included all the required content for one of one resident (R5). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: During the entrance conference on August 11, 2025, at approximately 9:40 a.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated the licensee provided medication management services to their residents, including medication set up. R5 was admitted on July 1, 2021, with diagnoses that included osteoarthritis (type of arthritis that occurs when flexible tissue at the ends of bones wears down). R5's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as service plan) dated June 10, 2024, indicated R5 received services to include weekly medication setup. R5's Order Summary Report dated August 1, 2025, included the following medications: -aspirin 81 milligrams; give one tablet by mouth in the morning (supplement) -atorvastatin 40 milligrams (mg); take one tablet by mouth at bedtime (cholesterol) -carvedilol 12.5 mg; take one tablet by mouth twice daily (blood pressure) -clonidine 0.3 mg; take one tablet by mouth every morning (blood pressure) -duloxetine 60 mg; take one capsule by mouth daily (depression) -furosemide 20 mg; take one-half tablet by mouth daily (diuretic) -hydralazine 25 mg; take on tablet by mouth three times a day (blood pressure) -hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg; take two tablets by mouth daily (blood pressure) -isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg; take one tablet by mouth once daily (chest pain) -oxybutynin 5 mg; take one-half tablet by mouth at bedtime (frequent urination) -pantoprazole sodium 40 mg; take one tablet by mouth once daily (reflux) -potassium chloride 20 milliequivalents (mEq); take one tablet by mouth twice daily (supplement) -ropinirole 1 mg; take one tablet by mouth at bedtime (restless legs) -sucralfate 1 gram (gm); take one tablet by mouth three times daily (stomach ulcers) R5's order summary report included a check mark next to each medication listed above indicating it had been set up. R5's record lacked documentation by the licensed nurse at the time of setup to include the name of medication, quantity of dose, times to be administered, and route of administration. On August 13, 2025, at 1:48 p.m., CNS-B stated R5's record did not include the required documentation for medication setup as listed above. CNS-B stated the overnight nurses set up medications for residents each week. The nurse would print the resident's order summary report and place a check mark next to each medication they setup. CNS-B stated she was not aware of the documentation requirements for medication setup. The licensee's Documentation of Medication Set-up policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated all medication setups will be documented immediately after preparation, verified against prescriber orders, and signed by the staff member performing the setup. No further information was provided. TIME PERIOD TO CORRECT: Seven (7) Days

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 10 Medication management for residents who will (2) for unplanned time away, when the pharmacy is not able to provide the medications, a licensed nurse or unlicensed personnel shall provide medications in amounts and dosages needed for the length of the anticipated absence, not to exceed seven calendar days; (3) the resident must be provided written information on medications, including any special instructions for administering or handling the medications, including controlled substances; and (4) the medications must be placed in a medication container or containers appropriate to the provider's medication system and must be labeled with the resident's name and the dates and times that the medications are scheduled. (b) For unplanned time away when the licensed nurse is not available, the registered nurse may delegate this task to unlicensed personnel if: (1) the registered nurse has trained the unlicensed staff and determined the unlicensed staff is competent to follow the procedures for giving medications to residents; and (2) the registered nurse has developed written procedures for the unlicensed personnel, including any special instructions or procedures regarding controlled substances that are prescribed for the resident. The procedures must address: (i) the type of container or containers to be used for the medications appropriate to the provider's medication system; (ii) how the container or containers must be labeled; (iii) written information about the medications to be provided; (iv) how the unlicensed staff must document in the resident's record that medications have been provided, including documenting the date the medications were provided and who received the medications, the person who provided the medications to the resident, the number of medications that were provided to the resident, and other required information; (v) how the registered nurse shall be notified that medications have been provided and whether the registered nurse needs to be contacted before the medications are given to the resident or the designated representative; (vi) a review by the registered nurse of the completion of this task to verify that this task was completed accurately by the unlicensed personnel; and (vii) how the unlicensed personnel must document in the resident's record any unused medications that are returned to the facility, including the name of each medication and the doses of each returned medication.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the licensee failed to ensure the registered nurse (RN) developed training and competencies for two of two unlicensed personnel (ULP-F and ULP-G) providing medications to residents for unplanned time away from home when the licensed nurse was not available. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at an isolated scope (when one or a limited number of residents are affected or one or a limited number of staff are involved, or the situation has occurred only occasionally). The findings include: ULP-F ULP-F was hired on December 2, 2024, to provide direct care and services to the licensee's residents. ULP-F's employee record lacked documentation of training and competencies for unplanned time away when the RN was not available. ULP-G ULP-G was hired on May 19, 2020, to provide direct care and services to the licensee's residents. ULP-G's employee record lacked documentation of training and competencies for unplanned time away when the RN was not available. On August 13, 2025, at 12:19 p.m., licensed assisted living director (LALD)-A and clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B reviewed ULP-F and ULP-G's employee records and stated they did not include documentation of training and competencies for providing medications to residents for unplanned time away. CNS-B stated both ULPs were trained and competent in unplanned time away; however, the documentation was not in their records. The licensee's Training on Unplanned Time Away policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated staff were educated in managing care for residents during absences, including medication packaging and instructions. No further information provided.

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 13 Prescriptions There must be a current written or electronically recorded prescription as defined in section 151.01, subdivision 16a, for all prescribed medications that the assisted living facility is managing for the resident.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure current written or electronically recorded prescriptions were obtained for all medications the licensee managed for three of four residents (R2, R3, and R4). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a pattern scope (when more than a limited number of residents are affected, more than a limited number of staff are involved, or the situation has occurred repeatedly; but is not found to be pervasive). The findings include: R2 R2 was admitted on October 14, 2024, with diagnoses that included diabetes. On August 12, 2025, at 7:24 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-F administer medications to R2. R2's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as the service plan) dated March 3, 2025, indicated R2 received services to include medication administration. R2's MAR dated August 2025, included the following medications: -glutose 15 Gel 40%; Take 15 grams (gm) by mouth as needed for low blood sugar and unable to safely drink (diabetes) R2's record lacked signed prescriber orders for the glucose gel. R3 R3 was admitted on January 15, 2024, with diagnoses that included dementia. R3's Service Plan Report dated May 14, 2025, indicated R3 received services to include medication administration. R3's MAR dated August 2025, included the following medications: -lorazepam 0.5 mg; take one tablet by mouth every six hours as needed for anxiety or restlessness -ondansetron 4 mg; take one tablet by mouth twice daily as needed (nausea) R3's record lacked signed prescriber orders for R3's lorazepam and ondansetron. R4 R4 was admitted on February 27, 2025, with diagnoses that included dementia. R4's Service Plan Report dated March 17, 2025, indicated R4 received services to include medication administration. R4's MAR dated August 2025, included the following medications: -acetaminophen 500 mg; take two tablets by mouth three times daily (pain) -citalopram 20 mg; take one tablet by mouth daily (depression) -Vitamin D3 50 mcg; take one tablet by mouth daily (supplement) R4's record lacked signed prescriber orders for R4's acetaminophen, citalopram and Vitamin D3. On August 13, 2025, at 1:25 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated R2, R3, and R4's record lacked signed prescriber orders for the medications listed above. The licensee's Medication Management Order policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated all orders must be clear, complete, and documented in the resident's medical record. Written orders must be signed by the prescriber, and telephone orders must be documented by a RN and signed by the prescriber with 72 hours. Any changes to medication orders will be communicated promptly to the pharmacy and relevant staff to prevent medication errors. The facility will adhere to all applicable 144G Assisted Living medication management regulations. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 14 Renewal of prescriptions Prescriptions must be renewed at least every 12 months or more frequently as indicated by the assessment in subdivision 2. Prescriptions for controlled substances must comply with chapter 152.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the facility failed to renew prescriptions at least every 12 months for one of four residents (R3). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at an isolated scope (when one or a limited number of residents are affected or one or a limited number of staff are involved, or the situation has occurred only occasionally). The findings include: R3 was admitted on January 15, 2024, with diagnoses that included dementia. R3's Service Plan Report dated May 14, 2025, indicated R3 received services to include medication administration. R3's record lacked evidence of prescriber orders being renewed annually for the following medications: -midodrine 2.5 mg; take one tablet by mouth twice daily. Hold for SBP greater than 150 (blood pressure), order dated May 30, 2024 -senna 8.6 mg; take one tablet by mouth every evening (constipation), order dated April 14, 2024 -Estrace vaginal cream 0.1 mg/gm; insert one gram vaginally in the evening every Monday and Thursday, order dated April 10, 2024 -fluticasone nasal spray 50 mcg/ACT; one spray in both nostrils in the morning (congestion), order dated June 17, 2024 -furosemide 20 mg; take one tablet by mouth daily (edema), order dated May 23, 2024 -Montelukast Sodium 10 mg; give one tablet by mouth at bedtime (asthma), order dated June 26, 2024 -omeprazole 20 mg; give one capsule by mouth in the morning (acid reflux), order dated April 14, 2024 -prednisone 10 mg; give one tablet by mouth in the morning every other day (steroid), order dated July 1, 2024 -arformoterol tartrate nebulizer 15 mcg/2 ml; inhale one vial via nebulizer two times daily (shortness of breath), order dated February 5, 2024 -budesonide inhalation suspension 0.25 mg/2 ml; inhale one vial via nebulizer tow times daily (allergies), order dated February 5, 2024 -Mucinex 600 mg; take one tablet by mouth two times a day (congestion/thick phlegm), order dated January 30, 2024 -albuterol sulfate inhaler; two puffs inhaled orally every six hours as needed (shortness of breath), order dated January 12, 2024 -benzonatate 100 mg; give one capsule by mouth every eight hours as needed (cough), order dated April 14, 2024 -Bisacodyl rectal suppository 10 mg; insert one suppository rectally every day as needed (constipation), order dated April 14, 2024 On August 13, 2025, at 1:20 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated R3's record lacked evidence of prescriber orders being renewed annually for the medications listed above. The licensee's Renewal of Prescription policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the facility would maintain systems and processes to track prescription renewal dates and will proactively coordinate with prescribers and pharmacies to ensure uninterrupted medication available The facility will comply with all applicable 144G Assisted Living medication management regulations. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 19 Storage of medications An assisted living facility must store all prescription medications in securely locked and substantially constructed compartments according to the manufacturer's directions and permit only authorized personnel to have access.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure all medications were securely locked in substantially constructed compartments and permitted only authorized personnel to have access. This had the potential to affect all residents. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: On August 12, 2025, at 7:24 a.m., the surveyor observed two medication carts located in dining room. Unlicensed personnel (ULP)-F removed a set of keys from a pen holder that was on top of the medication cart. ULP-F used the keys to unlock the medication cart and verified the narcotic count with ULP-E. ULP-F put the keys to the medication cart in his pocket .ULP-E then went to the second medication cart, removed a set of keys from a pen holder on top of the medication cart, unlocked the cart and verified the narcotic count with ULP-F. ULP-E put the keys to the medication cart back into the pen holder and stated ULP-G would get the keys when she arrived to start her shift. ULP-E stated the overnight shift kept the keys to each medication cart in the pen holders during their shift. On August 12, 2025, at 8:05 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-G unlocked the medication cart, removed R4's medication cards and compare each card to the medication order in the electronic medication administration record (EMAR) and place the medications into a medication cup. ULP-G brought R4's medications to him in the dining room leaving the medication cards on top of the medication cart, the drawer ajar and the keys in the lock. ULP-G returned to the medication cart with R4's medications after he refused to take them. ULP-G stated they were to attempt to give R4 his medications whole and if he refused then re-attempt with them crushed mixed in applesauce. ULP-G crushed R4's medications and went the kitchenette for applesauce and then to the dining room to administer the medications to R4. The medication cart remained unlocked, drawer ajar, keys in the lock and medication cards on top of the cart. ULP-G returned to the medication cart and put R4's cards back in the cart and started to prepare another resident's medications. On August 12, 2025, at 8:18 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-G prepare to administer medications to R3. ULP-G stated she had to check R3's blood pressure and pulse prior to administering her medications. ULP-G left R3's medications on the top of the medication cart, with the keys in the lock to check R3's blood pressure and pulse in the dining room. ULP-G returned to the medication cart, placed R3's blood pressure medication in the medication cup with the other medications and brought them to R3 in the dining room to administer. The medication cards remained on top of the cart, drawer was ajar, and the keys were in the lock. On August 13, 2025, at 12:43 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated the staff were trained to keep the medication cart locked when not in use and the keys should never be left in the pen holders or in the lock without staff present. The licensee's Medication Storage policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the licensee would store all medications in a secure, locked location, separate from food and other items. Controlled substances will be stored in a double-locked compartment. Medications requiring refrigeration will be stored in a locked refrigerator or locked box within a refrigerator. The facility will comply with all applicable 144G Assisted Living medication storage regulations. No further information provided.

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 20 Prescription drugs A prescription drug, prior to being set up for immediate or later administration, must be kept in the original container in which it was dispensed by the pharmacy bearing the original prescription label with legible information including the expiration or beyond-use date of a time-dated drug.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure accurate labeling for one of three residents (R2). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death), and was issued at an isolated scope (when one or a limited number of residents are affected or one or a limited number of staff are involved or the situation has occurred only occasionally). The findings include: R2 was admitted on October 14, 2024, with diagnoses that included diabetes. R2's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as the service plan) dated March 3, 2025, indicated R2 received services to include medication administration. R2's signed prescriber orders dated July 21, 2025, included: -Lantus Solostar Pen 100 units/milliliter (ml); inject 23 units daily at bedtime (diabetes) On August 12, 2025, at 9:14 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-F prepare to administer R2's Lantus insulin. The prescription label indicated to administer 18 units. The prescription label did not match the current prescriber order. On August 12, 2025, at 10:10 a.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated R2's dose had changed to 23 units and should have been a "directions changed refer to chart" sticker applied to the prescription label. The licensee's Medication Storage policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated all medications were labeled with resident name, medication name, dosage, route, frequency, and expiration date. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.71 Subd. 22 Disposition of medications (a) Any current medications being managed by the assisted living facility must be provided to the resident when the resident's service plan ends or medication management services are no longer part of the service plan. Medications for a resident who is deceased or that have been discontinued or have expired may be provided for disposal. (b) The facility shall dispose of any medications remaining with the facility that are discontinued or expired or upon the termination of the service contract or the resident's death according to state and federal regulations for disposition of medications and controlled substances. (c) Upon disposition, the facility must document in the resident's record the disposition of the medication including the medication's name, strength, prescription number as applicable, quantity, to whom the medications were given, date of disposition, and names of staff and other individuals involved in the disposition.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the licensee failed to document in the resident's record the disposition of the medications as required for one of one discharged resident (R6). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death), and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: R6 was admitted to the licensee on December 2, 2024, and discharged on June 10, 2025. R6's Medication Administration Record (MAR) dated June 2025, included the following medications: -acetaminophen 500 milligrams (mg); take two tablets by mouth twice daily (pain) -aspirin 81 mg; take one tablet by mouth with food (supplement) -atorvastatin 80 mg; take one tablet by mouth daily (cholesterol) -divalproex 500 mg; take one tablet by mouth twice daily -donepezil 5 mg; take one tablet by mouth for thirty days (dementia) -Fish Oil 1,000 mg; take two capsules by mouth daily (supplement) -gabapentin 100 mg; take one capsule by mouth at bedtime (pain) -levetiracetam 250 mg; take one tablet by mouth twice daily (depression) -lisinopril 2.5 mg; take one tablet by mouth daily (blood pressure) -melatonin 3 mg; take one tablet by mouth at bedtime (sleep) -paroxetine 10 mg; take one tablet by mouth at bedtime (depression) R6's Discontinued/Discharged Medication(s) Disposition form dated July 8, 2025, had seven columns that identified the medication name, strength/quantity, date filled, prescription number, disposal date, name of pharmacy and quantity. The prescription number and disposal date column were left blank. R6's record also contained a Discharged/Discontinued Medications document dated July 8, 2025, that identified which medications were sent with R6's family. The document did not include the prescription number as applicable or the disposal date. On August 13, 2025, at 12:49 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated they used the Discontinued/Discharge Medication(s) Disposition form to document the medication disposition upon discharge and then transfer that information into the electronic Discharged/Discontinued Medications document. CNS-B reviewed both documents and stated they did not include the required content as noted above. CNS-B stated she was not aware of the required content for documenting the disposition of medications. The licensee's Disposition of Medication policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the documentation record would include medication name, strength, quantity, date of disposal, method, and witness signatures. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.72 Subd. 3 Individualized treatment or therapy managemen For each resident receiving management of ordered or prescribed treatments or therapy services, the assisted living facility must prepare and include in the service plan a written statement of the treatment or therapy services that will be provided to the resident. The facility must also develop and maintain a current individualized treatment and therapy management record for each resident which must contain at least the following: (1) a statement of the type of services that will be provided; (2) documentation of specific resident instructions relating to the treatments or therapy administration; (3) identification of treatment or therapy tasks that will be delegated to unlicensed personnel; (4) procedures for notifying a registered nurse or appropriate licensed health professional when a problem arises with treatments or therapy services; and (5) any resident-specific requirements relating to documentation of treatment and therapy received, verification that all treatment and therapy was administered as prescribed, and monitoring of treatment or therapy to prevent possible complications or adverse reactions. The treatment or therapy management record must be current and updated when there are any changes.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to develop and implement a treatment or therapy management plan to include all required content for three of three residents (R1, R2, and R3). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a pattern scope (when more than a limited number of residents are affected, more than a limited number of staff are involved, or the situation has occurred repeatedly; but is not found to be pervasive). The findings include: R1 R1 was admitted on October 6, 2023, with diagnoses that included diabetes. On August 11, 2025, at 10:56 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-C check R1's blood sugar. R1's Service Plan Report dated March 4, 2025, indicated R1 received services to include bathing, dressing, suprapubic catheter (type of urinary catheter that is inserted through a small incision in the lower abdomen, just above the pubic bone, and into the bladder) care, safety checks, escorts, behavior monitoring, fall interventions and medication administration. R1's service plan did not include blood sugar checks. R1's signed prescriber orders dated July 12, 2025, included: -change BS (blood sugar) checks to after meals rather than with meals R1's Medication/Treatment/Therapy Management Plan dated October 14, 2024, indicated R1 did not have any treatment services. R1's record lacked a treatment management plan to include the following required content: - statement of the type of service that will be provided; - documentation of specific resident instructions relating to the treatments or therapy administration; - identification of treatment or therapy tasks that will be delegated to unlicensed personnel; - procedures for notifying a registered nurse or appropriate licensed health professional when a problem arises with treatments or therapy services; and - any resident-specific requirements relating to documentation of treatment and therapy received, verification that all treatment and therapy was administered as prescribed and monitoring of treatment or therapy to prevent possible complications or adverse reactions. On August 13, 2025, at 1:24 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B reviewed R1's Treatment Management Plan and stated blood sugar checks were not included. CNS-B stated she would update R1's treatment plan to include blood sugar checks. R2 R2 was admitted on October 14, 2024, with diagnoses that included diabetes. On August 12, 2025, at 7:24 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-F check R2's blood sugar. At this time the surveyor observed R2 wearing tubigrips (elastic bandage used to provide support and compression) on both lower legs. R2's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as the service plan) dated March 3, 2025, indicated R2 received services to include daily blood pressure checks, daily weights and blood sugar checks. R2's service plan did not include tubigrips. R2's signed prescriber orders included the following: -Daily weights; notify MD for a weight greater than 3 pounds daily or five pounds weekly, order dated October 16, 2024 -Blood Sugar checks twice daily, order dated October 23, 2024 -Tubigrips; apply tubigrips to bilateral lower extremities daily, remove at bedtime, order dated July 10, 2025 R2's record lacked prescriber orders for daily blood pressure checks. R2's Medication/Treatment/Therapy Management Plan dated October 14, 2024, indicated R2's only treatment was blood glucose monitoring. R2's record lacked a treatment management plan to include the following required content: - statement of the type of service that will be provided (daily weights, daily blood pressure checks and tubigrips) On August 13, 2025, at 1:26 p.m., CNS-B reviewed R2's Treatment Management Plan and stated R2's treatment plan should include daily weights, daily blood pressure checks and tubigrips. CNS-B stated the Treatment Management Plan document did not have an option to select for vital signs so had not included them in the treatment plan. CNS-B stated going forward she would select the "other" option and add vital signs in that area of the document. R3 R3 was admitted on January 15, 2024, with diagnoses that included dementia. On August 12, 2025, at 8:18 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-G check R3's blood pressure and pulse. R3's Service Plan Report dated May 14, 2025, indicated R3 received services to include bathing, grooming, dressing, toileting, escorts, transfers, mobility, fall interventions, behavior monitoring, medication administration. R3's service plan did not include daily blood pressure and pulse checks. R3's medication administration record (MAR) dated August 2025, included: -midodrine 2.5 milligrams (mg); take one tablet by mouth for hypotension (low blood pressure), HOLD for SBP greater than 150, check blood pressure and pulse at 8:00 a.m., and 4:00 p.m. R3's record lacked prescriber orders for daily blood pressure and pulse checks. R3's Medication/Treatment/Therapy Management Plan dated January 10, 2025, indicated R3 did not have any treatment services. R3's record lacked a treatment management plan to include the following required content: - statement of the type of service that will be provided; - documentation of specific resident instructions relating to the treatments or therapy administration; - identification of treatment or therapy tasks that will be delegated to unlicensed personnel; - procedures for notifying a registered nurse or appropriate licensed health professional when a problem arises with treatments or therapy services; and - any resident-specific requirements relating to documentation of treatment and therapy received, verification that all treatment and therapy was administered as prescribed and monitoring of treatment or therapy to prevent possible complications or adverse reactions. On August 13, 2025, at 1:28 p.m., CNS-B reviewed R3's Treatment Management Plan and stated it did not include daily blood pressure or pulse checks. CNS-B stated she would update R3's treatment plan by selecting the "other" option and add blood pressure and pulse checks. . The licensee's Individual Treatment and Therapy Management Plan policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the facility will develop, implement, ad regularly review individualized treatment, or therapy plans in collaboration with external therapy providers. Plans will be updated monthly, or more frequently as resident needs change, to ensure optimal outcomes. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.72 Subd. 6 Treatment and therapy orders There must be an up-to-date written or electronically recorded order from an authorized prescriber for all treatments and therapies. The order must contain the name of the resident, a description of the treatment or therapy to be provided, and the frequency, duration, and other information needed to administer the treatment or therapy. Treatment and therapy orders must be renewed at least every 12 months.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the licensee failed to ensure up-to-date written or electronically recorded orders were maintained for two of three residents (R2 and R3) receiving treatments. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death), and was issued at an isolated scope (when one or a limited number of residents are affected or one or a limited number of staff are involved or the situation has occurred only occasionally). The findings include: R2 R2 was admitted on October 14, 2024, with diagnoses that included diabetes. On August 12, 2025, at 7:24 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-F check R2's blood sugar. At this time the surveyor observed R2 wearing tubigrips (elastic bandage used to provide support and compression) on both lower legs. R2's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as the service plan) dated March 3, 2025, indicated R2 received services to include daily blood pressure checks, daily weights and blood sugar checks. R2's service plan did not include tubigrips. R2's signed prescriber orders included the following: -Daily weights; notify MD for a weight greater than 3 pounds daily or five pounds weekly, order dated October 16, 2024 -Blood Sugar checks twice daily, order dated October 23, 2024 -Tubigrips; apply tubigrips to bilateral lower extremities daily, remove at bedtime, order dated July 10, 2025 R2's record did not include a current order within the past 12 months for daily weights and blood sugar checks. R2's record lacked prescriber orders for daily blood pressure checks. R3 R3 was admitted on January 15, 2024, with diagnoses that included dementia. On August 12, 2025, at 8:18 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-G check R3's blood pressure and pulse. R3's Service Plan Report dated May 14, 2025, indicated R3 received services to include bathing, grooming, dressing, toileting, escorts, transfers, mobility, fall interventions, behavior monitoring, medication administration. R3's service plan did not include daily blood pressure and pulse checks. R3's medication administration record (MAR) dated August 2025, included: -midodrine 2.5 milligrams (mg); take one tablet by mouth for hypotension (low blood pressure), HOLD for SBP greater than 150, check blood pressure and pulse at 8:00 a.m., and 4:00 p.m. R3's record lacked prescriber orders for daily blood pressure and pulse checks. On August 13, 2025, at 1:34 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated R2's record lacked prescriber orders for daily blood pressure checks and R2's weight and blood sugar orders were not current within the last 12 months. CNS-B stated R3's record lacked prescriber orders for daily blood pressure and pulse checks. The licensee's Medication and Treatment Orders policy dated August 1, 2025, the facility will only perform treatments with a current, signed order from a licensed prescriber. Orders will be reviewed at least every 90 days or sooner if the resident's condition changes. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.82 Subd. 3 Policies (a) In addition to the policies and procedures required in the licensing of all facilities, the assisted living facility with dementia care licensee must develop and implement policies and procedures that address the: (1) philosophy of how services are provided based upon the assisted living facility licensee's values, mission, and promotion of person-centered care and how the philosophy shall be implemented; (2) evaluation of behavioral symptoms and design of supports for intervention plans, including nonpharmacological practices that are person-centered and evidence-informed; (3) wandering and egress prevention that provides detailed instructions to staff in the event a resident elopes; (4) medication management, including an assessment of residents for the use and effects of medications, including psychotropic medications; (5) staff training specific to dementia care; (6) description of life enrichment programs and how activities are implemented; (7) description of family support programs and efforts to keep the family engaged; (8) limiting the use of public address and intercom systems for emergencies and evacuation drills only; (9) transportation coordination and assistance to and from outside medical appointments; and (10) safekeeping of residents' possessions. (b) The policies and procedures must be provided to residents and the residents' legal and designated representatives at the time of move-in.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the licensee failed to ensure policies and procedures required in the licensing of assisted living facilities with dementia care were provided to each resident and the resident's legal/designated representative at the time of move-in for three of four residents (R1, R2 and R4) who resided in an assisted living with dementia care facility. This practice resulted in a level one violation (a violation that will cause only minimal impact on the resident and does not affect health or safety) and was issued at a pattern scope (when more than a limited number of residents are affected, more than a limited number of staff are involved, or the situation has occurred repeatedly; but is not found to be pervasive). The findings include: The licensee held an Assisted Living with Dementia Care license effective July 1, 2025, and was licensed for a bed capacity of 182 residents. R1 and R4 lacked evidence of receiving the required Assisted Living with Dementia Care policies and procedures at the time of resident move-in, to include: - philosophy of how services were provided based upon the assisted living facility licensee's values, mission, and promotion of person-centered care and how the philosophy shall be implemented; - evaluation of behavioral symptoms and design of supports for intervention plans, including nonpharmacological practices that were person-centered and evidence-informed; - wandering and egress prevention that provides detailed instructions to staff in the event a resident elopes; - medication management, including an assessment of residents for the use and effects of medications, including psychotropic medications; - staff training specific to dementia care; - description of life enrichment programs and how activities were implemented; - description of family support programs and efforts to keep the family engaged; - limited the use of public address and intercom systems for emergencies and evacuation drills only; - transportation coordination and assistance to and from outside medical appointments; and - safekeeping of resident's possessions. R2's record contained an Assisted Living with Dementia Care Policies Acknowledgment form signed on August 12, 2025, after the start of the survey. On August 13, 2025, at 1:34 p.m., licensed assisted living director (LALD)-A stated R1 and R4's record lacked evidence that they received the required dementia care policies and procedures. LALD-A stated R2's family was provided the dementia care policies and procedures and signed the acknowledgment form after the start of the survey. The licensee's Dementia Care policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the licensee would provide families with a copy of the facility's dementia care polices and procedures. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.40 Subdivision 1 Responsibility for housing and services The facility is directly responsible to the resident for all housing and service-related matters provided, irrespective of a management contract. Housing and service-related matters include but are not limited to the handling of complaints, the provision of notices, and the initiation of any adverse action against the resident involving housing or services provided by the facility.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to provide sufficient management, control, and operation of the housing and services provided by the facility. This had the potential to affect all residents. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death), and is issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: The licensee had an assisted living with dementia care license, effective July 1, 2025. The licensee's "Application for Assisted Living License", section titled "Official Verification of Owner or Authorized Agent", (page four and five of the application), identified an affirmative checkmark next to the statement, "I declare that, as the owner or authorized agent, I attest that I have read Minn. Stat. chapter 144G, and Minnesota Rules, chapter 4659, governing the provision of assisted living facilities, and understand as the licensee I am legally responsible for the management, control, and operation of the facility, regardless of the existence of a management agreement or subcontract." Another checkmark was noted at the statement, "I have examined this application and all attachments, and checked the above boxes indicating my review and understanding of Minnesota Statutes, Rules, and requirements related to assisted living licensure. To the best of my knowledge and believe, this information is true, correct and complete. I will notify MDH, in writing, of any changes to this information as required." Page six was electronically signed by the authorized agent on May 13, 2025. As a result of this survey, the following orders were issued under 0480, 0630, 0700, 0730, 0775, 0810, 1060, 1620, 1640, 1650, 1700, 1730, 1750, 1760, 1770, 1790, 1820, 1830, 1880, 1890, 1910, 1940, 1970 and 2110, which indicated the licensee's understanding of the Minnesota statutes were limited, or not evident for compliance with Minnesota Statutes, section 144G.01 to 144G.95.

defs.description: 144G.41 Subdivision 1 Subd. 1a (a-b) Minimum requirements; required food services (a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), food must be prepared and served according to the Minnesota Food Code, Minnesota Rules, chapter 4626. (b) For an assisted living facility with a licensed capacity of ten or fewer residents: (1) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part 4626.0033, item A, the facility may share a certified food protection manager (CFPM) with one other facility located within a 60-mile radius and under common management provided the CFPM is present at each facility frequently enough to effectively administer, manage, and supervise each facility's food service operation; (2) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part 4626.0545, item A, kick plates that are not removable or cannot be rotated open are allowed unless the facility has been issued repeated correction orders for violations of Minnesota Rules, part 4626.1565 or 4626.1570; (3) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part 4626.0685, item A, the facility is not required to provide integral drainboards, utensil racks, or tables large enough to accommodate soiled and clean items that may accumulate during hours of operation provided soiled items do not contaminate clean items, surfaces, or food, and clean equipment and dishes are air dried in a manner that prevents contamination before storage; (4) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part 4626.1070, item A, the facility is not required to install a dedicated handwashing sink in its existing kitchen provided it designates one well of a two-compartment sink for use only as a handwashing sink; (5) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, parts 4626.1325, 4626.1335, and 4626.1360, item A, existing floor, wall, and ceiling finishes are allowed provided the facility keeps them clean and in good condition; (6) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part 4626.1375, shielded or shatter-resistant lightbulbs are not required, but if a light bulb breaks, the facility must discard all exposed food and fully clean all equipment, dishes, and surfaces to remove any glass particles; and (7) notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part 4626.1390, toilet rooms are not required to be provided with a self-closing door.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure food was prepared and served according to the Minnesota Food Code. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: Please refer to the document titled, Food and Beverage Establishment Inspection Report (FBEIR) dated August 12, 2025, for the specific Minnesota Food Code violations. The Inspection Report was provided to the licensee within 24 hours of the inspection. TIME PERIOD FOR CORRECTION: Please refer to the FBEIR for any compliance dates.

defs.description: 144G.42 Subd. 6 (b) Compliance with requirements for reporting ma (b) The facility must develop and implement an individual abuse prevention plan for each vulnerable adult. The plan shall contain an individualized review or assessment of the person's susceptibility to abuse by another individual, including other vulnerable adults; the person's risk of abusing other vulnerable adults; and statements of the specific measures to be taken to minimize the risk of abuse to that person and other vulnerable adults. For purposes of the abuse prevention plan, abuse includes self-abuse.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure an individual abuse prevention plan (IAPP) was developed to include the required content for four of four residents (R1, R2, R3, and R4). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: R1 R1 was admitted on October 6, 2023, with diagnoses that included diabetes. On August 11, 2025, at 10:56 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-C check R1's blood sugar. R1's Service Plan Report dated March 4, 2025, indicated R1 received services to include bathing, dressing, suprapubic catheter (type of urinary catheter that is inserted through a small incision in the lower abdomen, just above the pubic bone, and into the bladder) care, safety checks, escorts, behavior monitoring, fall interventions and medication administration. R1's Vulnerability Assessment dated April 29, 2025, did not include the following required items: -the resident's susceptibility to abuse by another individual, including other vulnerable adults -statements of the specific measures to be taken to minimize the risk of abuse to that person and other vulnerable adults. R2 R2 was admitted on October 14, 2024, with diagnoses that included diabetes. On August 12, 2025, at 7:24 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-F administer medications to R2. R2's Visual/Bedside Individual Service Plan Report (also used as the service plan) dated March 3, 2025, indicated R2 received services to include dressing, escorts, fall interventions, mobility, transfers, grooming, toileting, behavior monitoring, safety checks, daily blood pressure checks, daily weights, blood sugar checks and medication administration. R2's Vulnerability Assessment dated April 29, 2025, did not include the following required items: -the resident's susceptibility to abuse by another individual, including other vulnerable adults -statements of the specific measures to be taken to minimize the risk of abuse to that person and other vulnerable adults. R3 R3 was admitted on January 15, 2024, with diagnoses that included dementia. On August 12, 2025, at 8:18 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-G administer medications to R3. R3's Service Plan Report dated May 14, 2025, indicated R3 received services to include bathing, grooming, dressing, toileting, escorts, transfers, mobility, fall interventions, behavior monitoring, medication administration. R3's Vulnerability Assessment dated May 14, 2025, indicated R3 was verbally aggressive towards others and did not pose a threat to other vulnerable adults. The licensee failed to recognize that R3 was at risk to abuse other vulnerable adults due to her verbal aggression. R3's Vulnerability Assessment failed to include the following required items: -the resident's susceptibility to abuse by another individual, including other vulnerable adults -statements of the specific measures to be taken to minimize the risk of abuse to that person and other vulnerable adults. R4 R4 was admitted on February 27, 2025, with diagnoses that included dementia. On August 12, 2025, at 8:05 a.m., the surveyor observed ULP-G administer medications to R4. R4's Service Plan Report dated March 17, 2025, indicated R4 received services to include bathing, fall interventions, safety checks, behavior monitoring, and medication administration. R4's Vulnerability Assessment dated April 29, 2025, indicated R4 was verbally aggressive towards others and did not pose a threat to other vulnerable adults. The licensee failed to recognize that R4 was at risk to abuse other vulnerable adults due to her verbal aggression. R4's Vulnerability Assessment failed to include the following required items: -the resident's susceptibility to abuse by another individual, including other vulnerable adults -statements of the specific measures to be taken to minimize the risk of abuse to that person and other vulnerable adults. On August 13, 2025, at 12:30 p.m., licensed assisted living director (LALD)-A and clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B reviewed R1, R2, R3 and R4's vulnerability assessment and stated it did not include the resident's susceptibility to abuse by another individual, including other vulnerable adults. LALD-A and CNS-B stated the licensee had recently updated the vulnerability assessment which included the option to assess the resident's susceptibility to abuse by others. However, the updated vulnerable assessment had not been completed for the residents yet. CNS-B confirmed R3 and R4 were verbally aggressive at times and would update their assessment to indicate that they are at risk to abuse other vulnerable adults. The licensee's Individual Abuse Prevention Plan (Vulnerability Assessment) policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the licensee would implement and IAPP for each resident as required under Minnesota Law. The IAPP shall identify specific resident vulnerabilities and outline individualized protective interventions to prevent abuse, neglect, and exploitation. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.43 Subdivision 1 Resident record (b) Resident records, whether written or electronic, must be protected against loss, tampering, or unauthorized disclosure in compliance with chapter 13 and other applicable relevant federal and state laws. The facility shall establish and implement written procedures to control use, storage, and security of resident records and establish criteria for release of resident information.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the licensee failed to ensure one of four residents (R3) personal health and medical information was kept private. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death), and was issued at an isolated scope (when one or a limited number of residents are affected or one or a limited number of staff are involved or the situation has occurred only occasionally). The findings include: On August 12, 2025, at 8:18 a.m., the surveyor observed unlicensed personnel (ULP)-G prepare to administer medications to R3. ULP-G logged into the I-Pad and pulled up R3's record, prepared the medications and went to the dining room to check R3's blood pressure and pulse. ULP-G left R3's record open on the I-Pad screen which was visible to other residents. ULP-G returned to the medication cart, documented R3's blood pressure and pulse on the I-Pad and then brought R3's medications to the dining room to administer. ULP-G left R3's record open on the I-Pad screen which was visible to other residents. On August 12, 2025, at 8:30 a.m., ULP-G stated they were supposed to log off or hide the I-Pad screen when not using the I-Pad to protect resident information. On August 13, 2025, at 12:40 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated all staff were trained to keep resident records confidential and private from any unauthorized individuals. The licensee's Record Keeping Requirements policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated records would be kept in a secure, confidential location with controlled access. Access would be provided to authorized personnel, residents, or legal representatives as required by law. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.43 Subd. 3 Contents of resident record Contents of a resident record include the following for each resident: (1) identifying information, including the resident's name, date of birth, address, and telephone number; (2) the name, address, and telephone number of the resident's emergency contact, legal representatives, and designated representative; (3) names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the resident's health and medical service providers, if known; (4) health information, including medical history, allergies, and when the provider is managing medications, treatments or therapies that require documentation, and other relevant health records; (5) the resident's advance directives, if any; (6) copies of any health care directives, guardianships, powers of attorney, or conservatorships; (7) the facility's current and previous assessments and service plans; (8) all records of communications pertinent to the resident's services; (9) documentation of significant changes in the resident's status and actions taken in response to the needs of the resident, including reporting to the appropriate supervisor or health care professional; (10) documentation of incidents involving the resident and actions taken in response to the needs of the resident, including reporting to the appropriate supervisor or health care professional; (11) documentation that services have been provided as identified in the service plan; (12) documentation that the resident has received and reviewed the assisted living bill of rights; (13) documentation of complaints received and any resolution; (14) a discharge summary, including service termination notice and related documentation, when applicable; and (15) other documentation required under this chapter and relevant to the resident's services or status.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the licensee failed to include the required content in a discharge summary for one of one discharged resident (R6). This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: R6 was admitted to the licensee on December 2, 2024, and discharged to a transitional care unit on June 10, 2025. R6's record included a Discharge Form dated July 3, 2025; however, it did not include the following required content: -a summary of the resident's stay that includes diagnoses, course of illnesses, allergies, treatments and therapies and pertinent lab, radiology, and consultation results; -a final summary of the resident's status from the latest assessment or review under Minnesota Statues, section 144G.70, if applicable, that includes the resident status, including baseline and current mental, behavioral, and functional status; -a reconciliation of all predischarge medications with the resident's post discharge prescribed and over-the-counter medications; and -a post discharge plan that is developed with the resident and, with the resident's consent, the resident's representatives, which will help the resident adjust to a new living environment. The post discharge plan must indicate where the resident plans to reside, any arrangements that have been made for the resident's follow-up care, and any post discharge medical and nonmedical services the resident will need. On August 13, 2025, at 12:40 p.m., clinical nurse supervisor (CNS)-B stated R6's discharge form did not include the required content as listed above. CNS-B and licensed assisted living director (LALD)-A stated they were not aware the discharge form the licensee used for all discharges did not include all the required content. The licensee's Discharge Summary policy dated August 1, 2025, indicated the licensee would provide a written discharge summary to the resident, the resident's legal representative, and/or the designated health care decision-maker in accordance with MN Statute 155G. The discharge summary would include: 1. Resident Identifiers: Name, date of birth, medical record number (if applicable). 2. Reason for Discharge: Brief statement describing the primary reason. 3. Summary of Services Provided: Overview of assisted living services received, including ADL support, medication management, and specialized care. 4. Current Health Status: Summary of diagnoses, recent vital signs, current functional status, and any significant changes. 5. Medication List: All current medications (prescription and over the counter), dosage, route, frequency, last administration time/date, allergies/adverse reactions. 6. Treatment Summary: Current treatments, therapies, and any outstanding physician orders. 7. Advance Directives: Code status and any documented health care directives. 8. Follow-Up Recommendations: Required follow-up care, upcoming appointments, therapy needs, and monitoring instructions. 9. Provider Contact Information: Primary care provider and other key specialist. 10. Facility Contact: Name and contact information of staff who prepared the summary. No further information was provided.

defs.description: 144G.45 Subd. 2. (a) Fire protection and physical environment Each assisted living facility must comply with the State Fire Code in Minnesota Rules, chapter 7511, and:
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on observation and interview, the licensee failed to comply with the current Minnesota Fire Code Provisions. This had the potential to directly affect all residents, staff, and visitors. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: During facility tour on August 13, 2025, from 9:10 a.m. through 11:17 a.m., with licensed assisted living director (LALD)-A, lead plant operations (LPO)-K, and intern (I)-L, the surveyor observed fire rated doors in the following locations that did not self-close, and latch as designed: Double 90-minute fire rated doors by resident room 269 did not fully close. The doors need adjustment. First and second flood trash chute did not latch. Double three-hour fire rated doors into the basement trash room were damaged and had the door closers removed. Double three-hour fire rated doors in the basement elevator lobby and basement hall leading from garage into elevator area were held open with toe kick devices. State Fire Code in MN Rules, chapter 7511 requires fire rated doors to be maintained to self-close and latch as designed. During same tour the surveyor observed the dryer vent was disconnected in the memory care laundry room. Dryer vents must be connected and kept clean to not create a fire hazard. LPO-K stated they would reconnect the vent. During same tour the surveyor observed exit signs that led into a fenced yard. The surveyor tried to exit through the door, but it was locked. LALD-A stated that the door had a delayed egress lock and would unlock if you push on it for 15 seconds. LALD-A pushed the door, and it released in 15 seconds. The door did not have sign on it that described the function of the door. The surveyor exited the building through the delayed egress door and observed two gates in the fence that were zip-tied shut. Emergency exits must provide unobstructed access to the public way. LALD-A and LPO-K discussed the options for the gates. LALD-A and LPO-K verified the above findings while accompanying on the tour and stated they understood the requirements.

defs.description: 144G.45 Subd. 2 (b-f) Fire protection and physical environment (b) Each assisted living facility shall develop and maintain fire safety and evacuation plans. The plans shall include but are not limited to: (1) location and number of resident sleeping rooms; (2) staff actions to be taken in the event of a fire or similar emergency; (3) fire protection procedures necessary for residents; and (4) procedures for resident movement, evacuation, or relocation during a fire or similar emergency including the identification of unique or unusual resident needs for movement or evacuation. (c) Staff of assisted living facilities shall receive training on the fire safety and evacuation plans upon hiring and at least twice per year thereafter. (d) Fire safety and evacuation plans shall be readily available at all times within the facility. (e) Residents who are capable of assisting in their own evacuation shall be trained on the proper actions to take in the event of a fire to include movement, evacuation, or relocation. The training shall be made available to residents at least once per year. (f) Evacuation drills are required for staff twice per year per shift with at least one evacuation drill every other month. Evacuation of the residents is not required. Fire alarm system activation is not required to initiate the evacuation drill.
defs.inspector_narrative: Based on interview and record review, the licensee failed to develop the fire safety and evacuation plan with required content, failed to provide the required training, and failed to conduct evacuation drills. This had the potential to directly affect all residents, staff, and visitors. This practice resulted in a level two violation (a violation that did not harm a resident's health or safety but had the potential to have harmed a resident's health or safety, but was not likely to cause serious injury, impairment, or death) and was issued at a widespread scope (when problems are pervasive or represent a systemic failure that has affected or has the potential to affect a large portion or all of the residents). The findings include: On August 13, 2025, at 11:20 a.m., licensed assisted living director (LALD)-A provided documents on the fire safety and evacuation plan (FSEP), fire safety and evacuation training, and evacuation drills for the facility. FIRE SAFETY AND EVACUATION PLAN The licensees FSEP titled, Fire Safety, undated, failed to include the following: The FSEP included standard resident evacuation procedures but failed to provide specific procedures for resident movement and evacuation or relocation during a fire or similar emergency including individualized unique needs of residents. LALD-A stated that the resident assessments were kept electronically. The FSEP failed to include any instructions for how staff are to access the assessments. TRAINING Record review indicated the licensee failed to provide evacuation training based on the fire safety and evacuation plan to employees, at hire and twice per year as evident by not providing documentation of training offered or training scheduled for a future date. LALD-A stated they provide training using a third-party computer-based training and during drills. There was no training provided to employees that was specific to the facility's FSEP and procedures. DRILLS The licensee failed to conduct evacuation drills for employees twice per year, per shift with at least one evacuation drill every other month. LALD-A stated they conduct drills every quarter throughout the year. LALD-A provided fire drill logs, but the logs failed to show that drills were conducted every other month. During an interview on August 13, 2025, at 11:56 a.m., LALD-A stated they understood the areas of the plan that needed to be updated.

summary_before: During a change of ownership inspection on April 15–16, 2026, the memory care community was found to have failed to conduct fire drills every other month within the memory care unit itself—one drill was held in a separate assisted living facility instead—and failed to provide fire and life safety training to staff on alternate months as required by Oregon Fire Code. The facility acknowledged these findings and stated it was implementing a Fire Drill & Life Safety Policy to ensure compliance going forward.
narrative:
Based on interview and record review, it was determined the facility failed to conduct fire drills every other month in accordance with the Oregon Fire Code (OFC) and failed to provide fire and life safety instruction to staff on alternate months. Findings include, but are not limited to: 

Fire and life safety documentation from 11/2025 through 03/2026 was reviewed on 04/15/26 with Staff 1 (ED), Staff 4 (Regional RN) and Staff 5 (Facility Maintenance Director). The following deficiencies were identified: 

* Two fire drills were conducted; however one of the simulated fire drills was conducted in the assisted living unit which is a separate licensed facility, not located within the MCC. Fire drills were not conducted in the MCC every other month, as required.  

* The facility provided one fire and life safety training for staff on 03/16/26. The facility failed to consistently provide fire and life safety training on alternate months of the fire drills, as required. 

During an interview on 04/15/26 at 10:25 am with Staff 1, she acknowledged the facility was still in the process of working on their systems for fire drills.  

The need to ensure fire drills and fire and life safety training were conducted per the OFC was reviewed with Staff 1, Staff 2 (Memory Care Director), Staff 3 (Health Services Director) and Staff 4 on 04/16/26 at 10:15 am. She acknowledged the findings.

OAR 411-054-0090 (1-2) Fire and Life Safety: Safety

(1) FIRE DRILLS. All fire drills shall be conducted according to the Oregon Fire Code (OFC). (a) Unannounced fire drills must be conducted and recorded every other month at different times of the day, evening, and night shifts. (b) Fire and life safety instruction to staff must be provided on alternate months. (c) The Fire Authority may develop an alternative fire drill plan for the facility. Any such plan must be submitted to the Department. (d) A written fire drill record must be kept to document fire drills that include: (A) Date and time of day; (B) Location of simulated fire origin; (C) The escape route used; (D) Problems encountered and comments relating to residents who resisted or failed to participate in the drills; (E) Evacuation time period needed; (F) Staff members on duty and participating; and (G) Number of occupants evacuated. (e) Alternate exit routes must be used during fire drills to react to varying potential fire origin points. (f) The evacuation capability of the residents and staff is a function of both the ability of the residents to evacuate and the assistance provided by the staff. (g) Staff must provide fire evacuation assistance to residents from the building to a designated point of safety as determined by the Fire Authority having jurisdiction. Points of safety may include, outside the building, through a horizontal exit, or other areas as determined by the Fire Authority having jurisdiction. (h) The fire alarm system shall be activated during each fire drill, unless otherwise directed by the Fire Authority having jurisdiction. (2) If the facility is unable to meet the applicable evacuation level, the facility must make an immediate effort to make changes to ensure the evacuation standard is met. Changes must include, but not be limited to: (a) Increasing staff levels, (b) Changing staff assignments, (c) Requesting change in resident rooms, and (d) Arranging for special equipment. After making necessary changes, if the facility fails to meet the applicable evacuation level, the facility must issue an involuntary move-out notice to the residents in accordance with OAR 411-054-0080.

(e) Alternate exit routes must be used during fire drills to react to varying potential fire origin points. (f) The evacuation capability of the residents and staff is a function of both the ability of the residents to evacuate and the assistance provided by the staff. (g) Staff must provide fire evacuation assistance to residents from the building to a designated point of safety as determined by the Fire Authority having jurisdiction. Points of safety may include, outside the building, through a horizontal exit, or other areas as determined by the Fire Authority having jurisdiction. (h) The fire alarm system shall be activated during each fire drill, unless otherwise directed by the Fire Authority having jurisdiction. (2) If the facility is unable to meet the applicable evacuation level, the facility must make an immediate effort to make changes to ensure the evacuation standard is met. Inspection Details: KIT014151
